**Jojo Designs/MuleSoft Partner Intro**
🕞 Started at 05:00 PM on 23 Jun, lasted 13m
data.raw_content:
## Action Items
- [ ]  Kailash to draft an SOW/SIRW and send it to Ryan for signature.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Kailash to have his team schedule an initial kickoff call.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Ryan to gather and compile documentation from the prior implementation partner to share with Kailash's team. 

## Key Points
- Purpose of the meeting: introduce Kailash (Dataskate) to Jojo Designs to help resolve MuleSoft compliance and integration issues left unresolved by a previous partner. 
- Jojo Designs had been overcapacity on MuleSoft flows, receiving overage notices, and a prior audit by Salesforce's Sam and Alicia identified flows to eliminate for compliance. 
- Previous implementation partner went dark on communication and their MuleSoft resource left the company, leaving the project ~95% complete with a few fixes and upgrades still outstanding. 
- Jojo Designs is on a MuleSoft Starter plan with 25 flows; duplicate flows (e.g., separate 3:00 PM and 9:00 AM data flows) are a key driver of the overage. 
- Kailash proposed a bucket-of-hours engagement model — 100 hours at $25/hour — to assess current flows, identify redundancies, and redesign the architecture to bring Jojo into compliance. 
- Scope of the engagement includes a full assessment of the current flow landscape, a proposed redesign, and an estimate of flows saved before development begins. 
- Ryan confirmed the approach makes sense and noted additional work may follow if the initial engagement goes well. 
- Discovery will require two initial sessions to understand the current landscape, data flow sequences, and dependencies between flows across systems. 
- Any documentation from the prior partner — including code base and implementation exchanges — will be shared to accelerate the assessment and architecture proposal. 
- Kailash will draft a Statement of Work, get it signed, and then schedule an initial kickoff call to begin the engagement.
